title: Oracle host simulation step
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, and let $C$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with at least one work tape. Choose states $en,ex$ of $C$, an oracle language $O\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$, a function $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and $a\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean word $z$, when $C$ starts in state $en$ with $z$ on tape $0$ and every other tape empty, there is a time $t\le a(\tau(|z|)+|z|+2)$ with $t>0$ such that it has not visited state $ex$ at any earlier time, and at time $t$ its configuration is the initial configuration in state $ex$ with the one-symbol word indicating whether $z\in O$ on tape $0$ and all other tapes empty. Now let $x$ be any Boolean input, let $c$ be any configuration of $M$ on input $x$, let $side\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and let $r\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume the query-tape head position is nonnegative when $side=\mathrm{true}$ and nonpositive when $side=\mathrm{false}$, its absolute value is at most $r$, the query string has length at most $r$, and query-tape cell $r$ is blank. Then, for some $u\le (2a+13)(r+1)+(2a+13)\tau(|Q|)$ if $c$ is in the query state, and $u\le(2a+13)(r+1)$ otherwise, the constructed host machine run from the stable encoding of $(c,side)$ reaches the stable encoding of $(M$'s one-step successor from $c$ relative to $O$, $side')$ for some $side'\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, where $Q$ is the query string on the query tape of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean oracle Turing machine
$C$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine and $C.k>0$
$O$ is a language over Boolean words

For every Boolean word $z$, the computation from the specified initial configuration reaches $ex$ at some positive time within the given bound, does not reach $ex$ earlier, and has the specified output configuration
$x$ is a Boolean input; $c$ is a configuration of $M$ on $x
$side$ gives the specified sign condition on the query-tape head position
The absolute query-tape head position is at most $r$
The query string length is at most $r$
